chapter_guidelines.content:
The ICD-10-CM provides codes for different types of myocardial 
infarction. Type 1 myocardial infarctions are assigned to codes I21.0-
I21.4. 
 
Type 2 myocardial infarction (myocardial infarction due to demand 
ischemia or secondary to ischemic imbalance) is assigned to code 
I21.A1, Myocardial infarction type 2 with the underlying cause coded 
first, if applicable. Do not assign code I24.89, Other forms of acute 
ischemic heart disease, for the demand ischemia. If a type 2 AMI is 
described as NSTEMI or STEMI, only assign code I21.A1. Codes 
I21.01-I21.4 should only be assigned for type 1 AMIs.  
 
Acute myocardial infarctions type 3, 4a, 4b, 4c and 5 are assigned to 
code I21.A9, Other myocardial infarction type. 
 
 
 
 
 
The "Code also" and "Code first" notes should be followed related to 
 
 
 
 complications, and for coding of postprocedural myocardial infarctions 
 
 
 
 during or following cardiac surgery.
chapter_guidelines.title: Other Types of Myocardial Infarction

chapter_guidelines.content:
infarction (STEMI) and non-
ST elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) 
The ICD-10-CM codes for type 1 acute myocardial infarction (AMI) 
identify the site, such as anterolateral wall or true posterior wall. 
Subcategories I21.0-I21.2 and code I21.3 are used for type 1 ST 
elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Code I21.4, Non-ST elevation 
(NSTEMI) myocardial infarction, is used for type 1 non-ST elevation 
myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) and nontransmural MIs. 
 
If a type 1 NSTEMI evolves to STEMI, assign the STEMI code. If a type 
1 STEMI converts to NSTEMI due to thrombolytic therapy, it is still 
coded as STEMI. 
 
For encounters occurring while the myocardial infarction is equal to, or 
less than, four weeks old, including transfers to another acute setting or a 
postacute setting, and the myocardial infarction meets the definition for 
“other diagnoses” (see Section III, Reporting Additional Diagnoses), 
codes from category I21 may continue to be reported. For encounters 
after the 4-week time frame and the patient is still receiving care related 
to the myocardial infarction, the appropriate aftercare code should be 
assigned, rather than a code from category I21. For old or healed 
myocardial infarctions not requiring further care, code I25.2, Old 
myocardial infarction, may be assigned.

Encounter Summary:
- Chart excerpt documents acute myocardial infarction with cardiology documentation of “NSTEMI.”
- Objective support in the excerpt includes “Troponin peaked at 4.2.”
- No diagnosis code is documented in the chart excerpt.

Documentation Gaps:
1. Gap: MI type specificity should be clarified only if not already intended as type 1.
   - Why it matters: ICD-10-CM I21.4 applies to type 1 NSTEMI; if the infarction is type 2 or another MI type, coding changes.
   - Evidence quote: “Patient with acute myocardial infarction. Cardiology note says ‘NSTEMI’.”
   - Additional coding guidance: ICD-10-CM guidance states “Code I21.4, Non-ST elevation (NSTEMI) myocardial infarction, is used for type 1 non-ST elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI)” and “If a type 2 AMI is described as NSTEMI or STEMI, only assign code I21.A1.”
   - Minimal clarification needed: Whether the documented NSTEMI represents type 1 NSTEMI versus another MI type, if this is not already clinically established elsewhere in the chart.

2. Gap: Timing/episode may need confirmation if the encounter is outside the acute MI reporting window.
   - Why it matters: Category I21 is used while the MI is 4 weeks old or less; after that, other coding may apply.
   - Evidence quote: “Patient with acute myocardial infarction.”
   - Additional coding guidance: “For encounters occurring while the myocardial infarction is equal to, or less than, four weeks old… codes from category I21 may continue to be reported.”
   - Minimal clarification needed: Whether this encounter is within 4 weeks of the acute MI, if the date/timeline is not otherwise documented.

Proposed Provider Queries:
1. Topic: Clarification of MI type
   - Reason query is needed: The excerpt supports NSTEMI, but ICD-10-CM assignment differs if the MI is type 1 versus type 2/other.
   - Evidence quote: “Patient with acute myocardial infarction. Cardiology note says ‘NSTEMI’. Troponin peaked at 4.2.”
   - Non-leading query text: “Based on the documented acute myocardial infarction, cardiology documentation of ‘NSTEMI,’ and troponin peak of 4.2, please clarify the type of myocardial infarction for this encounter, if known.”
   - Suggested response options:
     • Type 1 NSTEMI
     • Type 2 MI
     • Other MI type
     • Acute myocardial injury without myocardial infarction
     • Clinically undetermined
     • Other: _____
   - Compliance note: Use only if the broader chart leaves MI type unclear; do not query if type is already clearly documented elsewhere.

2. Topic: Acute timing of MI
   - Reason query is needed: ICD-10-CM category I21 depends on the MI being within the acute 4-week window.
   - Evidence quote: “Patient with acute myocardial infarction.”
   - Non-leading query text: “Please clarify whether the myocardial infarction being treated/monitored during this encounter is within 4 weeks of onset, if clinically known.”
   - Suggested response options:
     • Yes, within 4 weeks
     • No, more than 4 weeks from onset
     • Clinically undetermined
     • Other: _____
   - Compliance note: Only needed if encounter dates/onset timing are not already established in the chart.

Coding Specificity Checklist:
- MI type: type 1 vs type 2 vs other MI type
- NSTEMI vs STEMI status
- If STEMI, infarct site
- Whether the MI remains within the acute 4-week reporting window
- Whether any procedural/postprocedural MI context exists, if applicable elsewhere in chart

Risk Flags:
- Potential ambiguity: “NSTEMI” alone supports I21.4 only if it is type 1 NSTEMI per ICD-10-CM guidance.
- Insufficient evidence in the excerpt to query infarct site, coronary vessel, complications, or postprocedural MI.
- No contradiction is visible within the limited excerpt.
